legal_facts.statement: Anyone attending an open and public meeting of a local legislative body may record it, unless the body reasonably finds that the recording would persistently disrupt the meeting through noise, light or blocking the view.
Recording a confidential communication without the consent of every party to it is a crime in California; a communication in a public gathering or an open public proceeding is not confidential.

Anyone paid $1,000 or more in a calendar month to communicate with City officials to influence a City decision, or a salaried employee, officer or director of an organisation whose duties include doing so, is a local governmental lobbyist and must register with the Public Ethics Commission before lobbying.

A majority of a legislative body's members may not, outside a noticed meeting, use a series of communications of any kind, directly or through intermediaries, to discuss, deliberate or act on business within the body's jurisdiction.

Spending $1,000 or more in a calendar year on communications that expressly advocate for or against a clearly identified candidate or measure, not made at a candidate's or committee's behest, makes the spender a committee under the Political Reform Act.

A lawsuit arising from a statement made before, or about an issue under review by, a legislative, executive or judicial body, or in a public forum on an issue of public interest, may be met by a special motion to strike, filed within 60 days of service of the complaint.
